question: Should OpenClaw accept `currentTokenCount` and the token-budget helper exports as the stable public context-engine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold this into the broader assemble metadata RFC?
rationale: The patch expands the public plugin API and SDK exports on the same `ContextEngine.assemble` surface as an open RFC, so automation cannot choose the permanent contract direction.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Proof
options.body: Approve this API shape, then require redacted live long-session/context-engine proof before merge.

options.title: Fold Into Broader RFC
options.body: Pause this PR and handle token counts together with the broader assemble metadata proposal.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Avoid promoting the helper exports until the public SDK boundary is settled.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Proof
recommendation.body: Approve this API shape, then require redacted live long-session/context-engine proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman is the current assignee and the strongest feature-history owner for context-engine token budgeting and plugin SDK exposure.
